label: Topic
explain: Marks what the sentence is about. Usually goes first, but it is not wrong elsewhere. Think of it as pointing at the thing you want to talk about.

label: Doer
explain: Marks who does the action or what exists. Use it when the doer is new information or the answer to 'who?' / 'what?'.

label: Target
explain: Marks the object of the action: what you eat, buy, read, see. Also the place you move through or leave (道を歩く, 家を出る).

label: Goal / To
short: Destination, receiver, point in time, place where something is
explain: Marks the arrival point: where you go, who receives, when (clock time / day), and where something is or lives.

label: Place / By
short: Where the action happens, or the tool/means
explain: Marks the place where an action takes place (not where something merely is), and the means: by bus, with chopsticks, in Japanese.

label: With / And
explain: Marks the person you do something with, and joins two nouns (お茶とお菓子). Also marks what is said or thought (〜と言う).

label: Toward
explain: Marks the direction you head toward. Very close to に for destinations; へ stresses the direction, に the arrival. Either is fine in daily talk.

label: From
short: Starting point in place or time
explain: Marks where or when something starts: from Nara, from nine o'clock, from a friend.

label: Until / Up to
short: End point in place or time
explain: Marks where or when something ends: until five, up to the station. Often pairs with から.

label: Also
explain: Adds 'also'. It replaces は, が, を (私も, お茶も) and is added after に, で, と, へ, から, まで (奈良でも, 友達とも).
